nodes.label: L.exact — why a closed expression exists (keyed member form)
nodes.rationale: Grade PROVED, source M §11.7 with Freuder 1982, Rota 1964, Lauritzen 1996; depends on L.closed, L.tree, L.box, K.three, K.helly at depth 8.

nodes.label: Three separately necessary conditions for a closed product form
nodes.rationale: A closed form for |box ∩ Lambda| exists exactly when the constraint graph is a tree of monotone binary bounds: monotone bounds make the region a join- and meet-closed polytope, two-variable couplings make the graph a tree, and acyclicity lets the counting sum factorise with no term ever subtracted. Remove any one and no closed expression survives — each is exhibited with its own counterexample.

nodes.label: The conservation sum bound breaks join-closure
nodes.rationale: A ceiling on a sum rather than on a single coordinate records 89,864 join failures in 979,300 sampled composition pairs with meets unaffected; the two-line witness is a = (1,0,1) and b = (0,1,1), whose join transfers two units having removed one. Join-only failure because a maximum can breach a sum ceiling and a minimum cannot.

nodes.label: Closing the k-q-2S triangle returns the Rota sieve
nodes.rationale: Closing that cycle raises elimination width to two and forces an eight-term inclusion-exclusion; the tree-style count is then wrong by 40 cells on the witness box.
